fields.description: Smart Alerts are not going out today. I confirmed that Defrauded Customer and Shoplifting incidents are not generating any alerts. These were cases entered today. No matching known incident; nothing in the configuration or code we can read explains a tenant-wide stop, and the evidence that would settle it (today's alert run history and the notification logs) has not been read yet.

  • For this customer the alert is not sent by the screen the user saves on — the case screen hands off to a background job that calls back into the incident app to evaluate and email it; every hand-off in that chain logs quietly and never shows the user an error.

  • Each alert that actually gets evaluated writes a history row that is visible on the case, so today's cases will show directly whether the alerts were evaluated at all or were evaluated and simply not delivered.

Resolution summary, 9/28.

Issue:
From 9/24 11:06:43 UTC, Smart Alert runs for ADUSA, client 441, stopped completing. Runs reached "13a. Ready to send email" with no 13b, no insert into SmartAlertProcess and no End. InProcess stayed at 1, so every later save exited with "0. Quit ProcessSmartAlert because the smart alert for the case is still on processing". SmartAlertProcess had no rows after 9/24. Customer first noticed a case without alert around 4:20 PM ET on 9/24.

Checks along the way:
Infra, Russ Harmon on RETAILIT-20901, now Closed: SMTP relaying to SendGrid OK, API key valid, smartalert.email verified. SMTP now rejects emails over 25MB.
Kiran removed duplicate addresses from alert config 218 and manually triggered 9 cases on 9/27. The duplicates were not the cause.

Cause, per Kiran Vadday:
Deadlock in ProcessSmartAlert when processing runs in parallel under ADUSA traffic.

Fix:
PR 58273, one line change so a run waits for the previous one to finish. Validated in staging 9/27 23:56 UTC with 13b and a SmartAlertProcess row for ShopliftingID 1119654. Deployed to EU, then US prod on 9/28.

Verification:
Jim Cosseboom confirmed alerts from about 2:30 PM EDT 9/28. SmartAlertProcess rows with Success resumed from 19:30 UTC. Runs reach 13b and End.

Decisions:
Go forward only, requested by Jim. The fix does not reprocess stuck cases. A save does not trigger them while InProcess = 1. Any resend is manual: reset InProcess, trigger ProcessCaseAlert.aspx, check Grafana and SmartAlertProcess.

Related: RCS-29026, RETAILIT-20901. Same pattern on Vitamin Shoppe, client 433, RCS-29145.

🤖 Talos triage · confidence: medium

Talos can make mistakes. Please check important information.

Verdict — No evidence of a platform-wide fault: this account's payment-detail setup and the receipt screen's setup disagree about where the card brand is meant to come from, and one read of the transaction's payment rows will settle whether the brand reached us at all.

What we checked — We read this customer's receipt/detail screen and their payment-field setup. The receipt screen shows a card brand only from the standard card-brand field, and only for payments typed exactly as "credit"; separately, this customer — uniquely among all configured accounts — has a second, extra card-brand field set up for payments. That same screen already reads extra fields of this kind for product lines, fee lines and linked orders, but not for payments. We could not see the transaction data itself from here, so we cannot yet say whether the card brand arrived and sits in the extra field, or never arrived.

Next — Pull the payment rows for the example transaction 2609179617330521193 and check whether a card brand value is present and which of the two card-brand fields holds it; that single read separates "it never arrived" from "it arrived somewhere the receipt screen doesn't display". Worth also asking the customer whether tender detail was ever showing correctly, and since when.

Hello Jim Gould,

I have taken ownership of this ticket and will be investigating it for you. Please allow some time for me to research the issue and I will get back with you just as soon as I have any information.

Kind regards,

1. Environment and steps to reproduce

Environment: Production. Client 356, GPC. ARDM schema ardm_356 on GP11, replicated to Snowflake ARDMPROD.ARDM_356.

GPC (356), reported 24 Sep 2026 by SE Kristen Dyer

  1. Log in to the Portal in Production and go to Secure Store, Explorer.

  2. Open the search All Refunds by Cashier and run it for store CHA266.

  3. Open the receipt for Transaction ID 2609179617330521193, trading day 2026-09-17, ticket 533653.

Expected: a Visa tender line for 450.47 CR. GPC's own invoice shows Visa, 450.47 CR. Actual: the receipt has no tender line. Tender Type, Tender Card Number and Tender Amount are blank on every visible row of the 99 results, and the Tender Amount footer total is 0.00. Screenshots attached to the ticket by Kristen Dyer on 24 Sep.

2. Findings

All queries below are SELECT only, run by me on 24 Sep 2026.

Check

Result

TXN 2609179617330521193 in GP11 ardm_356

header 1, item 2, tender 0. Header matches the invoice: total -450.47, tax -28.48

Same TXN in Snowflake ARDMPROD.ARDM_356

header 1, item 2, tender 0. Replication is not the cause

Daily chain ratio, transactions with a tender row over headers

0.90 to 0.99 from 2026-04-15 to 2026-05-03. 0.577 on 2026-05-04

Same ratio in the windows checked after the break

2026-05-04 to 05-10, 07-01 to 08-03 and 09-12 to 09-20: between 0.35 and 0.77, with one outlier at 0.971 on 2026-05-09

Stores with zero tender rows, week of 2026-09-14

834 of 5,686 stores, 356,710 headers. Another 819 stores below 30%

Same check on GP11 clients 352 and 354 on 2026-05-01, 05-04 and 09-15

352 at 0.82, 0.80 and 0.77. 354 at 0.997, 0.997 and 0.998. No break on 05-04

ardm_header.totaltendercount is NULL on the example transaction and on every September header of its store except one, so the header does not tell us whether the POS sent a tender.

3. Troubleshooting performed, and the limits of support access

Claude flagged a tender load gap as the likely root cause, after a first Talos triage pointed to a display issue with a second card brand field. I checked the example transaction in GP11 and Snowflake, the daily tender to header ratio for the whole chain in the windows above, the per store coverage for one week, and the same ratio on clients 352 and 354. The display theory does not hold. There is no tender row to display. This is what I think is happening: since 2026-05-04 roughly 40% of GPC transactions load into ARDM without tender rows, and the gap now covers about 1,650 stores. Could someone else evaluate this and give me your thoughts?

No conversations outside this ticket so far.

Support cannot see the raw 356 input files, the pyardm load logs or the tender mapping for this client. That is where the cause sits, either the feed from GPC or the load step.

4. Still open

  1. Did anything change on 2026-05-04 in the 356 feed, the file layout or the pyardm tender mapping?

  2. Do the raw files for store CHA266 on 2026-09-17 carry the tender for ticket 533653?

  3. If the tender is in the raw files, can 2026-05-04 onward be reprocessed for 356?

  4. Is 2026-05-09 at 0.971 a partial reload, and does it point to the step that fails?

Related: https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-28632 covers the August backload for the same client 356. Priority High, opened 24 Sep 2026.

Hello @Jim Gould ,

Thank you for your patience while I looked into this, and thank you to Kristen for sending over such a clear example.

I was able to reproduce what you are seeing. The payment details for transaction 2609179617330521193 are not showing in Secure, and I have passed the ticket to the appropriate team for a closer review. I will update you here as soon as I hear back from them.

In the meantime, could you check with your team, whenever you have a moment, whether anything changed this year in how your stores process or send transaction data? A new register system or an update rolled out to some locations would both be helpful to know about.

Any detail you can share will help us narrow this down. I appreciate your help on this, and I will not leave you waiting.

Kind regards,
Juan

Root cause candidate: stale UTC timezone on migrated Incident-only accounts

Confirmed via membership.Users export for Vallarta. This is the same gap flagged on RCS-28065 (Ripp): IANA timezone is only written to the DB via an async ajax call fired from the user's browser on login. Incident-only tenants have no other path to set it, so any account that hasn't logged into the platform since cutover is still sitting on the UTC default written by the migration job.

Data (n=419 total accounts):

  • 308 accounts are TimeZone = UTC; all 308 have LastLoginDate = NULL (no login since migration).

  • 111 accounts show correct local TZ (mostly America/Los_Angeles); all 111 have a populated LastLoginDate.

  • Isolating just the migration batch (CreateDate = 2026-07-30 17:41:06.613, 305 accounts): 287 still UTC, 18 self-corrected after logging in. No accounts outside that pattern.

  • Case owner in the reported example (2026-ADUP-40-96, Fernando Torres) is in the 287: TimeZone = UTC, LastLoginDate = NULL.

This lines up with the reported symptom (alert delayed to the next day / inconsistent timing) — smart alert date-window logic evaluated against a UTC-context record vs. actual PT wall-clock time would explain exactly this behavior.

Requesting the same fix applied for Ahold (RCS-28030) and discussed for Stater Bros: bulk-update TimeZone to America/Los_Angeles in membership.Users for the affected Vallarta accounts, rather than waiting on individual logins to self-correct. Emma Gomez escalated to Support on Aug 7 to get this unblocked so United can finish test verification and schedule the production cutover.

Actions needed:

  1. Confirm current SSO config on the Appriss/SP side for the unitedsupermarkets tenant, verify the ACS URL and Entity ID being presented match what the new apprissretail.com domain expects.

  2. Get Albertsons' SSO/IdP team (Lakshmi Priya Nair / Greeshma George, per the thread) to confirm they've updated their IdP metadata with the new ACS URL and Unique Identity URL, this was asked for repeatedly and never confirmed.

  3. Reproduce the SAML error with Marcus Young (or ask for a fresh screenshot/error trace) — the original error screenshot referenced in the email isn't visible in the ticket text, so you'll want that to diagnose the actual SAML failure (e.g., audience mismatch, ACS mismatch, cert issue).

  4. Once config is verified/corrected, have Marcus re-test login at the test URL and confirm Incident + related modules load properly.

  5. Reply on the ticket to Emma Gomez with a status update, she's asked twice now for someone to take ownership.

  6. Once test SSO is confirmed working, coordinate the production migration window with Kathleen Garner (CSM) per the original migration plan.

Correction

The SSO Response Log path proposed on August 12 does not apply to this symptom. The Response Log only records claims that reach the Appriss SAML endpoint. Both errors below occur inside Azure Entra ID before the request reaches Appriss.

Environment

Test. test.apprissretail.com/unitedsupermarkets/signin/sso/saml2.

Findings

Screenshot dated April 16, 2026, correlationId d16aa739-36b4-412c-af2c-5787b5afcae4. Error AADSTS650059. App 4faf29ab-110f-4978-b042-5c8c2714d6fb is not configured for tenant b7f604a0-00a9-4188-9248-42f3a5aac2e9. SignInAudience is set to AzureADMyOrg, which restricts the app to a single tenant.

Second screenshot, same session. Error AADSTS700016. The application identifier https://test.apprissretail.com/unitedsupermarkets was not found in directory Safeway, Inc. The sign in request resolved against the wrong Azure AD tenant.

Neither error reaches the SAML claim mapping stage. This rules out a claim configuration issue on the Appriss side.

Reviewed the two screenshots against the SSO Response Log documentation. No claim mapping test run, the errors predate that stage. No conversation held outside the ticket.

Ruled out. Do not repeat

Claim field mapping on the Appriss SSO tab. The request never reaches that stage. SAML certificate expiration. AADSTS650059 and AADSTS700016 are Azure AD tenant resolution errors, not certificate errors.

Still open

  1. Confirm which Azure AD tenant hosts the unitedsupermarkets service principal, the unified tenant b7f604a0-00a9-4188-9248-42f3a5aac2e9 or Safeway Inc.

  2. Confirm the app registration is consented in that tenant.

  3. Confirm which tenant Marcus Young's sign in request resolves against today.

  4. Once tenant routing is corrected, request a fresh login attempt and a new screenshot.

Reporter Emma Gomez has waited 33 days without an owner confirming this diagnosis. Route the customer update in parallel, not after these four items close.

1. Correction

None. No previous statement on this ticket needs correction.

2. Environment and steps to reproduce

Environment: APIS Production, 7-Eleven tenant, Company ID 7-eleven.

7-Eleven, case CA-44541-COR-2026-0001, verified live today

  1. Log in to APIS PROD as jbarber.

  2. Open the case through All Event Search, Store 44541.

  3. Open the Case Type field dropdown on the case form.

  4. Look at the list of selectable values.

Expected: COR listed as a selectable Case Type value, matching the value already stored on the case.
Actual: The dropdown lists only Corporate, External, Franchise, Labor/Tips/Subpoena, Vendor/Contractor. COR is not among them. A separate checked row reading star COR renders above the list, outside it, to represent the value already stored on the record. Screenshot attached to this ticket.

Corp_Internal_Theft_Fraud report, ID 5165, test copy ID 5511

  1. Duplicate report 5165 into a test copy, ID 5511, to avoid touching the client's live report.

  2. Open Configure filters on the copy.

  3. Change the case.event_type filter comparison operator to CONTAIN, then to IN.

  4. Open the Operand selector for that filter under each operator.

Expected: COR available as an operand value, or a free text option, so the filter can include it alongside Corporate.
Actual: The Operand control is a fixed picklist under every operator tried. It lists only Corporate, External, Franchise, Labor/Tips/Subpoena, Vendor/Contractor. COR is never offered. Screenshots attached.

3. Findings

  • Verified: on CA-44541-COR-2026-0001, the stored Case Type value COR does not exist in the case side picklist. Live dropdown, 9/15.

  • Verified: the AdHoc report Operand for case.event_type pulls from that same picklist regardless of comparison operator. Tested CONTAIN and IN on report copy 5511.

  • Verified: filtering on case.iice_id with CONTAIN and a free text operand returns no additional cases. That field is most likely the internal numeric case ID, not the displayed Case ID string.

  • Unverified, from AI triage, listed so it is not re-explored: the root cause is the incident to case elevation step copying the incident's short type code into the case Case Type field without mapping it to a valid case side value.

  • Precedent, RCS-1508: in 7-Eleven, the Event Type field on screen maps to event_sub_type in the filter, not event_type. Confirms field naming in this tenant is not literal.

4. Troubleshooting performed, and the limits of support access

Claude flagged this as the likely root cause. I checked it myself against the live case and the report builder, and here is what I found. This is what I think is happening. Could someone else evaluate this and give me your thoughts?

I logged into APIS PROD myself and opened the case, the dropdown and the report builder directly, step by step, as described above. I do not have access to the elevation logic itself or to the underlying tables that would confirm where the incident's type code gets written to the case record. That is what Engineering access would confirm.

No conversations happened outside this ticket about this specific finding today.

5. Ruled out. Do not repeat

  • Report level workaround via CONTAIN or IN on case.event_type. Operand is picklist bound, COR is not a member by definition.

  • Free text filter on case.iice_id. Field does not hold the visible Case ID string.

  • Self defined SQL style field in the report builder. Not attempted, out of scope for Support without Engineering sign off on a client owned report.

6. Still open

  1. Confirm whether the elevation logic is copying the incident type code without mapping it, as observed on this one case.

  2. If confirmed, provide an estimate for a data level correction and whether it needs a one time backfill for cases already affected.

  3. Confirm how many cases across 7-Eleven currently carry an invalid Case Type value like this one, if that is queryable faster on your side than through the report builder.

  4. This is currently a Critical client escalation. Please advise on timeline as soon as you have one, even a rough one.
